steps.note: One step. Until a withdrawal exists a departed student continues to be invoiced, marked absent, alerted on and counted on the section roster (BR-1) — but raising it closes nothing on its own.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A withdrawal with no reason is not raised at all.
plan.atomicity: One write: the withdrawal and the audit entry together or not at all. **Nothing closes.** The student stays enrolled, on the roster and invoiced until clearance runs and the withdrawal is approved (BR-4, BR-10). The reason decides which certificates are issued and whether a later re-admission is permitted (BR-3) — which of the reasons permit one is not decided anywhere in this use case.

parameters.name: route

parameters.name: reason
parameters.type: enum: Transfer to another school | Family relocating | Financial | Disciplinary | Deceased
parameters.notes: Why the student is leaving (BR-3, E1). It decides which certificates are issued and whether a later re-admission is permitted, so it is never inferred from the route.

parameters.name: intended_leaving_date

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

planningRules.rule: Never infer the route. A family that applied, a school that acted for non-payment and a student who simply did not return are three different records (BR-2), and the third must not be omitted because it is the quietest.

Never choose the reason. It decides which certificates are issued and whether the child can ever come back (BR-3) — and "Disciplinary" in particular is a decision taken through the expulsion route, not a label applied here.
Never describe a raised withdrawal as closing anything. The student stays enrolled, on the roster, invoiced and expected in attendance until clearance runs and it is approved (BR-1, BR-4, BR-10).

Report the fee position, the credit, the deposit and the property outstanding. Clearance is the point at which the school still has standing to ask (BR-4), and the family should know what it involves before the leaving date.

Never plan a write-off. A balance written off rather than collected is raised and approved under the write-off use case by the approver named there — a withdrawal must not become a route around that control (BR-6, E5).
Report re-admission as derived and undecided. The reason determines it (BR-3), but which reasons permit one is not stated anywhere in this use case.

reversal.statement: A withdrawal is never deleted (BR-12, E8). One raised in error is returned unapproved or cancelled, and the record stays — results, the fee ledger, ledger entries and audit trails all reference the student.

steps.note: A return is not a cancellation. The two lead to different states.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report the difference before acting: returning sends it back to be corrected and raised again, while cancelling ends it and leaves the student enrolled with the withdrawal on record. Either way nothing is deleted — and if the family is staying, cancelling is what they mean.
